title: The Armenian Catholics
hookLine: heirs of the first nation to adopt Christianity

cards: "The ark rested … upon the mountains of Armenia." That's Genesis, in the Douay-Rheims, at the end of the flood. Noah's boat comes to rest, and the name on the map is Armenia.
Armenians call a great snow-capped mountain on their horizon Ararat, and tradition ties it to that story.
But the story at the center of Armenian Christianity comes much later, and it begins in a pit: a man thrown into a deep hole by a king, and left there to die.

teach.b: Armenian tradition tells of Gregory, a Christian who served at the royal court and refused to worship the old gods.
The king had him tortured and thrown into a pit, where, the story goes, he survived for years, fed in secret by a kind woman. Then the king fell gravely ill, and no one could heal him.

Gregory was brought up out of the pit, prayed over the king, and the king was healed and baptized. Armenians call him Saint Gregory the Illuminator, the one who brought light. Then the claim in today's line.
Armenians say that when their king was baptized, the kingdom became Christian with him, so they speak of Armenia as the first nation to adopt Christianity.
It's a claim at the heart of how Armenians see themselves; historians discuss the details, and others make claims of their own. Then the alphabet.
Tradition says a monk named Mesrop created the Armenian letters so the Bible could be read in Armenian, and the script is still in use today.

teach.h: THEIR OWN LETTERS, THEIR OWN LITURGY.
teach.b: A people with their own scripture in their own letters. Last, the Armenian Catholics.
The ancient church of the Armenian people is the Armenian Apostolic Church.
Some Armenian communities came into communion with Rome and became the Armenian Catholic Church, praying the same Armenian liturgy, with the same saints, the same music, the same letters.
Armenians have known great suffering, and their churches, Apostolic and Catholic, have gone into exile together and prayed for the same dead.

how: Armenian Catholics celebrate the Armenian Divine Liturgy in Classical Armenian, sharing its music, saints and feasts with the Armenian Apostolic Church, and honor Saint Gregory the Illuminator as the one who brought the faith to Armenia.

games.q: you're Gregory, brought up from years in a pit. the king who put you there is sick and asks for your help. what do you do?
o: refuse, and let him face what he deserves.
pray over the king who imprisoned you.
games.why: in the Armenian tradition, Gregory prays over the king, the king is healed and baptized, and Armenians tell this as the start of their Christian nation.

practice: Picture a stone church on a high plateau, a mountain white against the sky, an old woman lighting a thin candle in sand, and families scattered far from those mountains who still teach their children the letters.
If you pray, pray for Armenia and its people, near and far. If you don't, simply honor them: a people who kept a faith, a liturgy and an alphabet through a great deal.

wordCard.voice: The Armenian Catholics. Armenians in communion with Rome who pray the ancient Armenian liturgy and honor Saint Gregory the Illuminator, heirs of what Armenians call the first Christian nation. Today's word.

orig.note: Armenian: Armenia, as Armenians name their country, in the letters tradition credits to Mesrop.

carryVoice: Your line: the first nation. A story that began in a pit ended with a light-bringer. I'll be here tomorrow.
